doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Influences: Lena Horne, Dinah Washington, Little Jimmy Scott
summary: She names where her gowns, humor and phrasing came from.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Did you learn anything when you were in an audience that you actually were conscious about?

No. Because I don’t – if you notice, I haven’t mentioned any singers except Al Hibbler. I didn’t really get to see female singers. I didn’t really see what they did, other than to know that Lena Horne was Lena Horne and to hear the humor in Dinah Washington’s records. I was already signed with Capitol Records when I met Dinah Washington.
So there are people that influenced your style. I think you’ve referred to it in that past, maybe, as osmosis. But, looking back, what do you see in you that came from - places?

Okay, the gowns, the style, the look – Lena Horne. The humor on the floor, Dinah Washington. The sound is Little Jimmy Scott. The phrasing and all that’s Little Jimmy Scott, to me. I heard – I loved him. I loved to hear Jimmy sing. I only heard him. I never saw him until last – when we brought him out to California. I never saw Little Jimmy Scott perform. I heard him, but I never got to see him perform until way late.
